title: GPU hotspot eviction & soft-shed playbook for hosted API capacity exhaustion
creator: Nina Kaur
description: After a production incident on 2026-03-02 where a combination of long-context image-to-text workloads and a sudden tenant spike led to GPU pool exhaustion, queues built up and the hosted API experienced elevated latency and soft-failures. This ticket tracks follow-ups: implement a hotspot-aware eviction policy, measurable soft-shed policy (tiered degradation + deterministic fallbacks), improved prewarm/priming heuristics, and telemetry + synthetic tests to prevent regressions. Goal: reduce outage window and provide predictable, graceful degradation for affected tenants.
action_items: Design & implement hotspot eviction: track per-GPU hot-keys (kv-cache pressure) and evict low-priority KV entries when pool pressure > 80% (ENG-branch: feature/gpu-hot-evict)
Soft-shed policy prototype: earliest-response path that reduces per-request kv/cache prefetch and falls back to shorter context model variant; implement canary via route-level rollout
Admission scoring change: incorporate sequence-length histogram and recent tokens/second into admission score to avoid sudden sequence-length-driven pack amplification
Autoscaler tuning: add a prewarm signal derived from tenant sustained qps spikes and forecasted demand (30s smoothing), plus lower hysteresis for emergency scale-up
Telemetry & alerting: new Grafana dashboard panels for per-pool kv-cache hit/miss ratio, per-tenant average sequence length, queue growth rate, and 'eviction events' metric
Synthetic test harness: daily long-context spike test targeting hosted pools with a controlled tenant to surface regressions
Runbook & playbook: publish a one-page Rapid Containment Runbook for on-call with step-by-step containment actions and tenant messaging snippets
acceptance_criteria: Implemented hotspot eviction logic behind feature flag and validated in staging (no regressions on throughput)
Canary soft-shed policy running on 5% of traffic with clear telemetry showing reduced queue growth and reduced 95th pct latency during controlled spikes
Autoscaler responds to synthetic long-context spike within target SLO (scale-up within 90s) in staging
Dashboards and alerts created with runbook links and annotated incident timelines
Post-deploy postmortem test plan created and assigned to SRE for weekly validation

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive eviction reduces immediate queue pressure but can increase cold-start latency and slightly degrade tail-quality for some tenants. We will gate aggressive thresholds behind tenant-prioritization and feature flags. Engineering will document ABI/contract for model-variant fallbacks so client SDKs can be informed of structured degradations.
postmortem_summary: The incident exposed an interaction between model rollout (larger KV footprints), tenant spike, and autoscaler hysteresis. Immediate mitigations (throttles + emergency scale) restored availability; however, this ticket packages long-term mitigations: hotspot eviction, soft-shed policies, autoscaler signal improvements, and better telemetry + synthetic tests.
